essence: Word-meditation timed to meaning aims at all-lord.
Self needs neither knowing nor action: world void.
No bondage, no freedom: terrors reflections in water.
Senses left: self-abiding abides in own self.
One-nature lighting all: knowing and known one vision.
Yoked here: IS Bhairava; speech curser-and-favorer.

rasa.dominant: śānta with vīra undertow (stillness that ends in sovereignty)
rasa.justification: The block is denial-then-claim: no bondage, no freedom, no inner-making — and then the sudden sovereign claim, speech that curses and blesses: quiet resolving into authority, not agitation.

sections.SUMMARY: Conviction completes the earlier denial: I-and-mine emptied, supportless mind falls calm; word-meditation timed to meaning aims at all-lord; the net-question resolved from firmness yields calm; self needing neither knowing nor action makes world void of both; bondage, freedom, terrors all reflections in water; senses left, self-abiding abides; one-nature lighting all gives single vision; the fourfold wasted yields Bhairava-form; a hundred-plus-twelve told in brief makes the knower-person; and yoked here one IS Bhairava whose speech performs curse and favor alike.
sections.FUNCTION: Clears the last metaphysical obstacles, then flips into sovereign identity — quiet as power.
sections.KEY TERMS: pratipatti (conviction as mechanism); śabda-abhyāsa (word-meditation); prati-bimba (reflection-model of bondage); caturka (the fourfold); sāmānya-saṃvid (one-nature lighting).
sections.LOCAL CONTEXT: Closes the teaching-section; the fruit-praise and japa-counts follow (p15).
sections.BOUNDARY: The hundred-plus-twelve count is recension-sensitive (flagged in argmap) — never used to force dhāraṇā numbering.
sections.EXPLANATION: Three sūtra-pairs do final demolition: conviction removes the last holding ('I-mine-this'), word-meditation converts speech into aimed aim at the all-lord, and the net-question dissolves into firmness-given calm. Then the old question of agency returns — self needs no knowing, no action, so world-possessions are void — and bondage, freedom and terrors are all dismissed as reflections (sun in water). With the senses left, only self-abiding remains; one-nature lights knowing and known into a single vision; the fourfold (manas, consciousness, power, self) wasted gives Bhairava-form. The count-vows: hundred-plus-twelve in brief for the knower. And the turn: yoked here, one IS Bhairava — the text's highest authority — whose speech now performs curses and favors without remainder.
sections.RELATED: Count (100+12) vs Hareesh's 116 practice-verses framing — flagged, not reconciled; sovereign-speech = sāmraṭ-bhāva, cf. Śivasūtra sovereignty themes.
